def test_all_prefixes():
    # Basic case
    assert all_prefixes("abc") == ["a", "ab", "abc"]

    # Empty string returns empty list
    assert all_prefixes("") == []

    # Single character
    assert all_prefixes("a") == ["a"]

    # Longer string
    assert all_prefixes("hello") == ["h", "he", "hel", "hell", "hello"]

    # String containing spaces (prefixes must include them)
    assert all_prefixes("ab cd") == ["a", "ab", "ab ", "ab c", "ab cd"]

    # Special characters
    assert all_prefixes("!@#") == ["!", "!@", "!@#"]

    # Numeric characters
    assert all_prefixes("123") == ["1", "12", "123"]

    # Result length equals input string length
    assert len(all_prefixes("python")) == 6

    # Prefixes are ordered from shortest to longest
    result = all_prefixes("prefixes")
    lengths = [len(p) for p in result]
    assert lengths == sorted(lengths)

    # First prefix is the first char, last prefix is the full string
    for s in ["abc", "hello", "x"]:
        prefixes = all_prefixes(s)
        assert prefixes[0] == s[0]
        assert prefixes[-1] == s

    # Each prefix is a prefix of the next one
    prefixes = all_prefixes("chain")
    for i in range(len(prefixes) - 1):
        assert prefixes[i + 1].startswith(prefixes[i])

from typing import List


def all_prefixes(string: str) -> List[str]:
    
    result = []

    for i in range(len(string)):
        result.append(string[:i+1])
    return result
